**Reginald Fils-Aimé** (/ˈfiːsəmeɪ/ *FEE-sə-may*;[[2]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-MTV_Multiplayer-2) born March 25, 1961) is an American businessman best known for being the [president](President_(corporate_title) "President (corporate title)") and [chief operating officer](Chief_operating_officer "Chief operating officer") of [Nintendo of America](Nintendo_of_America "Nintendo of America"), the North American branch of the Japanese video game company <Nintendo>, from 2006 to 2019. Prior to his promotion to president and COO, Fils-Aimé was Executive Vice President of Sales and Marketing.

Fils-Aimé gained celebrity status among gamers following his appearance at Nintendo's [E3 2004](E3_2004 "E3 2004") press conference in May 2004, and helped to revitalize Nintendo's image as a major contender among the other video game console makers, [Sony Interactive Entertainment](Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment") and <Microsoft>. Fils-Aimé had held previous sales and marketing executive roles at [Procter & Gamble](Procter_%26_Gamble "Procter & Gamble"), [Pizza Hut](Pizza_Hut "Pizza Hut"), <Guinness>, [Derby Cycle](Derby_Cycle "Derby Cycle"), [Panda Express](Panda_Express "Panda Express"), and <VH1>.

Fils-Aimé retired as president of Nintendo of America on April 15, 2019 after an announcement on February 21, and was succeeded by [Doug Bowser](Doug_Bowser "Doug Bowser"). He subsequently became a Leader in Residence at [Cornell University](Cornell_University "Cornell University") and later named to the Board of Directors for [Brunswick Corporation](Brunswick_Corporation "Brunswick Corporation"), <GameStop>, and [Spin Master](Spin_Master "Spin Master").

## Early life

Fils-Aimé has said that he adopted his optimistic attitude from his mother. He was raised on [Long Island](Long_Island "Long Island"),[[1]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-Seattle_Times-1) where he attended [Brentwood High School](Brentwood_High_School_(New_York) "Brentwood High School (New York)");[[4]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-VideoGamer-4) he described himself as the "lone minority" among his classmates.[[5]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-New_York_Times-5) He was accepted into [Cornell University](Cornell_University "Cornell University") in 1979,[[5]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-New_York_Times-5) and graduated with a [Bachelor of Science](Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") in [applied economics](Applied_economics "Applied economics") and management from the [College of Agriculture and Life Sciences](Cornell_University_College_of_Agriculture_and_Life_Sciences "Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences") in 1983.[[6]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-Cornell_Alumni-6) He was president of the school's [Phi Sigma Kappa](Phi_Sigma_Kappa "Phi Sigma Kappa") fraternity chapter,[[6]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-Cornell_Alumni-6) where he was described as being neat and organized.[[1]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#c

**Kenneth A. Williams** (born October 30, 1954) is an American [game programmer](Game_programmer "Game programmer") who co-founded [On-Line Systems](Sierra_Entertainment "Sierra Entertainment") together with his wife [Roberta Williams](Roberta_Williams "Roberta Williams"). On-Line Systems eventually became Sierra On-Line and was ultimately renamed [Sierra Entertainment](Sierra_Entertainment "Sierra Entertainment"). The couple were leading figures in the development of [graphical adventure games](Graphic_adventure_game "Graphic adventure game"). At its height, Sierra employed nearly 1,000 people prior to its acquisition in 1996.

## History

### Early years

Williams was born in October 30, 1954 in [Evansville, Indiana](Evansville%2C_Indiana "Evansville, Indiana")[[1]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-HistoryLink-1) and later grew up in [Simi Valley, California](Simi_Valley%2C_California "Simi Valley, California"). Ken and Roberta's early contributions to the computer game industry were partially chronicled in the book *[Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution](Hackers%3A_Heroes_of_the_Computer_Revolution "Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution")*. He wrote the textbook *Apple II Computer Graphics*,[[2]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-2) and articles for *[Softline](Softline_(magazine) "Softline (magazine)")*.[[3]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-williams198109-3)

### Sierra On-Line

Main article: [Sierra On-Line](Sierra_On-Line "Sierra On-Line")

Williams and wife Roberta co-founded On-Line Systems in 1979. Sierra's notable online service, the [ImagiNation Network](ImagiNation_Network "ImagiNation Network"), was purchased by AT&T in 1994.[[4]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-4) Williams was the president of Sierra until the company was sold to [CUC International](CUC_International "CUC International") in July 1996, but he remained with the company leading its strategic direction until November 1997. <Vivendi> (now [Activision Blizzard](Activision_Blizzard "Activision Blizzard") after the [Vivendi Games](Vivendi_Games "Vivendi Games") and <Activision> merger) currently holds the [Sierra](Sierra_Entertainment "Sierra Entertainment") name.[[5]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-5)

In his role as Sierra's CEO, Williams focused on innovation: "I'm not sure how typical I am of other CEOs ...most of my time is spent looking at product ... To me, everything is about being able to build awesome product ... Any game which does not push the state of the art leaves an opportunity for a competitor's game to look better."[[6]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-6)

In Sierra's later years, the company's focus had shifted to publishing many titles from other studios, including [Valve](Valve_Corporation "Valve Corporation")'s *[Half-Life](Half-Life_(video_game) "Half-Life (video game)")*. Commenting on [first-person shooters](First-person_shooter "First-person shooter"), Williams recalls, "By the time I decided we wanted into the genre, we were too far behind. With 20/20 hindsight, I blew it when I had the chance to buy [id](Id_Software "Id Software") and didn't ... Valve was the first group I had spoken with that could put Sierra in front of id."[[7]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-7)

Williams has cited <Microsoft> and [The Walt Disney Company](The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") as influencing Sierra's business model. "These two companies were our role models. I read every book written on both companies. I did everything to try to understand how they thought, and how they did business."[[8]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-8)

### Recent years

After a spell of being inactive in the computer game industry, in 2022, it was reported that he was currently working with his wife Roberta on a new VR and flatscreen version of *Colossal Cave 3D Adventure*, a redux of the text-adventure title from 1977.[[9]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-9) Prior to this, he had focused on writing and managing a Web site construction tool called Talkspot,[[10]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-10) which

**Reginald Fils-Aimé** (/ˈfiːsəmeɪ/ *FEE-sə-may*;[[2]](Reggie_Fils-Aim%C3%A9#cite_note-MTV_Multiplayer-2) born March 25, 1961) is an American businessman best known for being the [president](President_(corporate_title) "President (corporate title)") and [chief operating officer](Chief_operating_officer "Chief operating officer") of [Nintendo of America](Nintendo_of_America "Nintendo of America"), the North American branch of the Japanese video game company <Nintendo>, from 2006 to 2019. Prior to his promotion to president and COO, Fils-Aimé was Executive Vice President of Sales and Marketing.

Fils-Aimé gained celebrity status among gamers following his appearance at Nintendo's [E3 2004](E3_2004 "E3 2004") press conference in May 2004, and helped to revitalize Nintendo's image as a major contender among the other video game console makers, [Sony Interactive Entertainment](Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment") and <Microsoft>. Fils-Aimé had held previous sales and marketing executive roles at [Procter & Gamble](Procter_%26_Gamble "Procter & Gamble"), [Pizza Hut](Pizza_Hut "Pizza Hut"), <Guinness>, [Derby Cycle](Derby_Cycle "Derby Cycle"), [Panda Express](Panda_Express "Panda Express"), and <VH1>.

Fils-Aimé retired as president of Nintendo of America on April 15, 2019 after an announcement on February 21, and was succeeded by [Doug Bowser](Doug_Bowser "Doug Bowser"). He subsequently became a Leader in Residence at [Cornell University](Cornell_University "Cornell University") and later named to the Board of Directors for [Brunswick Corporation](Brunswick_Corporation "Brunswick Corporation"), <GameStop>, and [Spin Master](Spin_Master "Spin Master").

Fils-Aimé has said that he adopted his optimistic attitude from his mother. **Kenneth A. Williams** (born October 30, 1954) is an American [game programmer](Game_programmer "Game programmer") who co-founded [On-Line Systems](Sierra_Entertainment "Sierra Entertainment") together with his wife [Roberta Williams](Roberta_Williams "Roberta Williams"). On-Line Systems eventually became Sierra On-Line and was ultimately renamed [Sierra Entertainment](Sierra_Entertainment "Sierra Entertainment"). The couple were leading figures in the development of [graphical adventure games](Graphic_adventure_game "Graphic adventure game"). At its height, Sierra employed nearly 1,000 people prior to its acquisition in 1996.

## History

### Early years

Williams was born in October 30, 1954 in [Evansville, Indiana](Evansville%2C_Indiana "Evansville, Indiana")[[1]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-HistoryLink-1) and later grew up in [Simi Valley, California](Simi_Valley%2C_California "Simi Valley, California"). Ken and Roberta's early contributions to the computer game industry were partially chronicled in the book *[Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution](Hackers%3A_Heroes_of_the_Computer_Revolution "Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution")*. He wrote the textbook *Apple II Computer Graphics*,[[2]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-2) and articles for *[Softline](Softline_(magazine) "Softline (magazine)")*.[[3]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-williams198109-3)

### Sierra On-Line

Main article: [Sierra On-Line](Sierra_On-Line "Sierra On-Line")

Williams and wife Roberta co-founded On-Line Systems in 1979. Sierra's notable online service, the [ImagiNation Network](ImagiNation_Network "ImagiNation Network"), was purchased by AT&T in 1994.[[4]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-4) Williams was the president of Sierra until the company was sold to [CUC International](CUC_International "CUC International") in July 1996, but he remained with the company leading its strategic direction until November 1997. <Vivendi> (now [Activision Blizzard](Activision_Blizzard "Activision Blizzard") after the [Vivendi Games](Vivendi_Games "Vivendi Games") and <Activision> merger) currently holds the [Sierra](Sierra_Entertainment "Sierra Entertainment") name.[[5]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-5)

In his role as Sierra's CEO, Williams focused on innovation: "I'm not sure how typical I am of other CEOs ...most of my time is spent looking at product ... To me, everything is about being able to build awesome product ... Any game which does not push the state of the art leaves an opportunity for a competitor's game to look better."[[6]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-6)

In Sierra's later years, the company's focus had shifted to publishing many titles from other studios, including [Valve](Valve_Corporation "Valve Corporation")'s *[Half-Life](Half-Life_(video_game) "Half-Life (video game)")*. Commenting on [first-person shooters](First-person_shooter "First-person shooter"), Williams recalls, "By the time I decided we wanted into the genre, we were too far behind. Valve was the first group I had spoken with that could put Sierra in front of id."[[7]](Ken_Williams_(game_developer)#cite_note-7)

Williams has cited <Microsoft> and [The Walt Disney Company](The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") as influencing Sierra's business model. "These two companies were our role models.
